basics.name: Taleef Tamsal
basics.label: Software Developer · LLM Safety and Evaluation Researcher
basics.summary: I build production AI, backend, and healthcare software, and I research LLM safety and evaluation. At Medical Informatics Engineering I'm the sole developer of a production healthcare platform. I'm first author on four papers, including an oral presentation at a NeurIPS 2026 workshop and a Findings of AACL-IJCNLP 2026 paper.

work.name: Medical Informatics Engineering
work.summary: Sole developer of WorkWell Measure Studio, a full-stack healthcare compliance platform that runs CMS FHIR/CQL measure logic and keeps the evidence behind each computed result.
highlights: Encoded nine CMS clinical quality measures with HL7 FHIR R4 and SMART Backend Services. All 455 official MADiE test cases pass, and I reported a reference-engine defect that its maintainers confirmed.
Scaled the platform to 72,100 outcomes across 5,000 subjects, with CI/CD and 3,268 automated backend tests.
Traced a four-day production outage to its root cause and cut idle queries from about 1,300 a day to 2.
Moved manual drafting and evidence review into AI-assisted workflows through 13 role-gated tools, while deterministic logic still decides every sensitive result.

work.name: Purdue University Fort Wayne
work.position: Graduate Researcher, AI Safety and LLM Evaluation, and Teaching Assistant
work.summary: Studied how LoRA, QLoRA, 4-bit quantization, and full fine-tuning change jailbreak robustness in open-weight LLMs, advised by Dr. Jonathan Rusert. Also worked as a graduate teaching assistant.
highlights: Fine-tuned and evaluated 25 LLM configurations across five model families (4B to 14B parameters) with SLURM on A100 and A30 GPUs.

Used a pre-specified ±5 pp equivalence test (TOST) to show that LoRA and full fine-tuning degrade black-box jailbreak safety equivalently under a controlled recipe, across nearly 600 attack-success measurements.
Ran a 750-sample blind human annotation study. GPT-4o-mini mislabeled 45.7% of safe outputs as jailbreaks, against 8.6% for a calibrated classifier, which inflated measured degradation by about 3x.
For the JUDGe study, showed that GPT-5.6 judges still over-flagged 21.5–29.9% of safe completions and gave identical outputs different labels on 3–15% of repeat evaluations.

work.name: Riccle (early-stage e-commerce startup)
work.summary: Ran operations reporting and analytics for a small e-commerce team.
highlights: Merged order, inventory, payment, and customer data from four separate trackers into one source and built recurring KPI reports with SQL and Python, saving about six hours a week.

work.name: Purdue University Fort Wayne
work.position: Research Collaborator, Query-Efficient Adversarial NLP (Dr. Jonathan Rusert's group)
work.summary: Studied where black-box text attacks such as TextFooler and TextBugger spend their query budget, separating word selection from replacement and comparing datasets, victim models, and attack traces to find where fewer queries would do the same job.

work.name: Medical Informatics Engineering
work.position: Software Development Intern, NLP and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
work.summary: Built and containerized the first prototype of RASS, a RAG platform for semantic search over 3,000+ Redmine issues, with hybrid search, reranking, and MCP and SSE interfaces.
highlights: Benchmarked relevance, grounding, and latency across retriever and model settings, and load-tested the service at 25 concurrent users and AI agents with responses under 500 ms.
Added OpenTelemetry tracing so retrieval and service failures were easy to diagnose.
